commit_subject: (screen-flagged) Unsure (promote pattern): rewrites existing DE pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml (315 lines) and removes known-validation-gaps entry.
description: The RuleSpec applies the complete 30 Del. C. section 1102(a)(14) rate schedule to separate-return Person-grain taxable-income candidates and the combined TaxUnit-grain candidate, then selects the same pre-credit branch as pinned PolicyEngine-US 1.752.2.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module encoded no part of the section 1102(a)(14) schedule and instead computed tax as a caller-supplied cumulative base plus a caller-supplied marginal rate above a caller-supplied floor, then subtracted a caller-supplied section 1110 "personal credit" and a section 1108 standard deduction whose cited provisions carry no operative text in the certified corpus slice, so the encoded liability rested on values and a credit branch with no basis in the cited source.
triage.triage_notes: Provisions read through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-snap-2026-07-21). Verified: (1) section 1102(a)(14) text matches the post-fix parameters exactly - 2.2% over $2,000 to $5,000, 3.9% to $10,000, 4.8% to $20,000, 5.2% to $25,000, 5.55% to $60,000, 6.6% above $60,000; (2) the pre-fix proof excerpt for de_pit_pilot_schedule_tax was "tax table income", a phrase that occurs in section 1102 ONLY in subsection (d) (the Director-prescribed alternative tax tables), not in the subsection (a) schedule the formula purported to implement - the post-fix re-grounds the atoms on the (a)(14) text and declares (d) under deferred_outputs; (3) us-de/statute/30/1108 resolves to the bare stub text '§ 1108' and us-de/statute/30/1110 to '§ 1110 § 1111 § 1112 § 1113' in the certified slice, so the pre-fix excerpts "the standard deduction of a resident individual" and "personal credits" appear nowhere in their cited sources. Corroborating: the commit removes this module's entry from known-validation-gaps.yaml, whose header reads "Modules failing encode validate (source grounding etc.)", and the PR records "validation-gap ratchet: resolved Delaware waiver retired; validation pass". Competing reading a reviewer should weigh: this is a screen-flagged promote-pattern rewrite (315 lines, whole module replaced), and much of the change is added scope rather than correction - it moves to Person-grain separate returns plus a combined branch, adds the de_pit_pilot_taxpayer_of_tax_unit data_relation, and retargets the output from after-credit liability (compared to de_income_tax_before_refundable_credits) to pre-nonrefundable-credit schedule tax (de_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits_unit); the rule name de_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability is retained but now means pre-credit tax. If a reviewer counts only the added scope, this is 'unclear'; I classified fidelity because the removed credit branch and the supplied-schedule formula were ungrounded in the cited source as certified. Also note two non-fidelity deltas: every version gains effective_to 2026-12-31 (pre-fix windows were open-ended), which is a campaign fail-closed convention narrower than the statute's own "For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2013", not a source correction; and de_pit_pilot_files_separately, de_pit_pilot_taxpayer_is_included, de_pit_pilot_supplied_separate_taxable_income and de_pit_pilot_supplied_combined_taxable_income remain undeclared caller-supplied inputs. Commit also rewrote the companion test file (194 lines), the encoding manifest, and the reverse index; PR #980 has an empty commit body and no review comments (the review cycle is summarized in the PR body only).
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a promote-pattern scope expansion, and the refutation only partly lands: the pre-fix module's operative content really did rest on values and a branch with no basis in the cited source, and the fix removes and re-grounds them. Pre-fix, the liability was `max(0, schedule_tax - de_pit_pilot_supplied_nonrefundable_credit)` where schedule_tax was `supplied_bracket_base + supplied_marginal_rate * max(0, TI - supplied_bracket_floor)` — a one-bracket linear function whose every number came from the caller, proof-grounded on citations that carry no operative text in the certified slice (I resolved us-de/statute/30/1108 → body "§ 1108", 6 chars; us-de/statute/30/1110 → "§ 1110 § 1111 § 1112 § 1113", 27 chars), while the schedule atom's excerpt "tax table income" comes from § 1102(d), the Director-prescribed-table subsection, not the (a) rate schedule it purported to implement. The fix deletes the 1108/1110 citations and the credit subtraction, encodes all six (a)(14) rates and ceilings as parameters with verbatim excerpts from the resolved § 1102(a)(14) text, flips `upstream_source_check.status` from `composed_from_supplied_current_authority` to `official_parameter_source`, and retires this module's entry from `known-validation-gaps.yaml` under the header "Modules failing encode validate (source grounding etc.)" — documentary confirmation the pre-fix module was on record as failing source grounding. It is a fidelity correction of the untraceable/ungrounded kind, though confidence is held at 0.6 because the commit and PR use only promotion language and a large share of the same diff is genuine new scope.

triage.verifier_notes:
Refutation attempts and why they fall short, for the reviewer to weigh:
(1) "Promote pattern, not a fix." The commit subject is "Promote Delaware 2026 income tax schedule" with an empty body, and the PR body never says anything was wrong — its "Review cycle" section lists only presentation/provenance and branch-shape findings. Real counter-pressure, but the PR does record "validation-gap ratchet: resolved Delaware waiver retired", and the deleted `known-validation-gaps.yaml` entry for `us-de/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml` sits under `validate_failures:` whose file header reads "Modules failing encode validate (source grounding etc.)". Caveat: that waiver list is a bulk consolidation-time burn-down (every entry points at the same issue 782, same owner, same 2026-10-08 expiry), so it is not a targeted finding about this module.
(2) "The pre-fix boundary was declared, so nothing false was claimed." The old rationale did say the floor/base/rate/deduction/credit "are declared caller-supplied inputs" and that "The pipeline adds no numeric literals of its own". But the encoded function is still not § 1102(a)(14): outside the six pinned grid cases it returns `base` even for taxable income below the supplied floor, and the companion test had to hand-feed floor 25,000 / base 1,001 / 0.0555 (and 60,000 / 2,943.5 / 0.066) per case. The schedule was outside the encoding, not encoded.
(3) "Provenance only, therefore mechanical." Does not hold: formulas, parameters, entity grain (new Person-grain rules and a `de_pit_pilot_taxpayer_of_tax_unit` data_relation), and version windows (`effective_to: '2026-12-31'` added) all change. This is far more than excerpt or citation strings.
(4) Alternative kinds considered. `unrepresented_clause` is arguable — the source states a six-band schedule the encoding lacked and the fix adds it — but the fix's center of gravity is removing/re-grounding ungrounded values and the 1110 credit branch, so untraceable_branch fits at least as well and the kind definition explicitly covers "formulas grounded on the wrong provision." `wrong_entity_or_scope` describes a real change (TaxUnit-only → Person+TaxUnit, output moved from after-nonrefundable-credits to `de_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits_unit`) but nothing in the source made the old scope wrong; that is consequence, not defect.
(5) Honest residual: note that §§ 1108 and 1110 do exist in real Delaware law, so the old outline (AGI − standard deduction, tax − personal credit) is not contrary to Delaware statute as such; what it lacked was any basis in the *cited corpus source*. A reviewer who reads "cited source" as the statute rather than the certified slice could downgrade this to unclear or not_a_defect. The new module also stops modeling the deduction and credit entirely, so this is a boundary redraw as much as a correction.
Corpus evidence is reproducible: resolver returned corpus_release us-rulespec-snap-2026-07-21, provision file data/corpus/provisions/us-de/statute/2026-07-13-recovery.jsonl, with § 1102(a)(14) text matching every new parameter excerpt verbatim ("2.2% of taxable income in excess of $2,000 but not in excess of $5,000" … "6.6% of taxable income in excess of $60,000") and rates 0.022/0.039/0.048/0.052/0.0555/0.066 and ceilings 2000/5000/10000/20000/25000/60000 all correct.
